hero.headline: Federal Reserve expected to hold rates steady at first meeting under new chairman
hero.body:
The Federal Reserve is widely expected to maintain interest rates at its meeting today, marking the first policy decision under newly confirmed Chairman Kevin M. Warsh. The decision comes as the central bank faces significant political pressure and questions about its independence.

Warsh, who served as a Fed governor from 2006 to 2011, recently won Senate confirmation after a contentious process. His appointment has drawn scrutiny due to his alignment with President Donald Trump's calls for lower interest rates. In a Wall Street Journal opinion piece last November, Warsh criticized the Fed's leadership as "broken" and said the institution's reach had "extended far beyond its grasp."

The political backdrop to Warsh's appointment is substantial. Trump has pressured the Federal Reserve to reduce rates and has engaged in an unprecedented legal battle with the central bank. A criminal investigation was launched against outgoing Chair Jerome Powell over budget overruns in Fed headquarters renovations, though the Justice Department ended that investigation after a Republican senator threatened to block Warsh's nomination. Powell announced he would remain on the Fed's board as a governor until the renovation inquiry concludes "with transparency and finality."

In his final press conference as chair, Powell expressed deep concern about threats to the Fed's independence. "The institution is being battered over these things," Powell said. "We're having to resort to the courts to enforce our ability to make monetary policy without political considerations."

Despite Democratic concerns that Warsh would become Trump's "sock puppet" at the central bank, Warsh told the Senate he would be an "independent actor" as Fed chair. Powell said he would "take him at his word" regarding Warsh's commitment to resist political pressure.

The Fed faces a complex economic landscape as it determines its policy path forward. Market observers expect the rate decision to maintain current policy as officials continue evaluating economic conditions. Stock index futures have risen ahead of the announcement, reflecting investor expectations for a steady outcome.

Investors will closely examine not only the rate decision but also the accompanying policy statement and any remarks from Warsh for signals about future policy direction. The new chairman has an opportunity to establish his leadership approach and clarify the Fed's thinking to markets and the public.

The meeting carries symbolic weight beyond the technical aspects of monetary policy. Powell's pointed warnings about political interference underscore concerns among Fed officials about maintaining the institutional independence necessary for sound economic stewardship. How Warsh navigates the tension between his stated commitment to independence and the administration's interest rate preferences will likely define his tenure at the central bank.

cards.headline: G7 Leaders Endorse U.S.-Iran Agreement at France Summit
cards.body:
Leaders from the Group of 7 nations praised a preliminary agreement between the United States and Iran at a summit in France, calling it a breakthrough secured under President Trump's leadership. The endorsement came as G7 officials gathered for talks that have included efforts to build closer ties with the U.S. administration.

The agreement represents a shift in U.S.-Iran relations, though the specific terms of the preliminary deal were not detailed in the announcement. G7 leaders, representing the United States, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and the United Kingdom, issued statements highlighting the diplomatic progress achieved through the negotiations.

The summit in France has served as a platform for allied nations to engage with President Trump on matters of international diplomacy and security. The Iran agreement emerged as a central topic of discussion, with leaders characterizing it as a significant step forward in addressing tensions that have persisted between Washington and Tehran.

The preliminary nature of the agreement suggests that further negotiations will be required to finalize the terms. The G7's collective support signals broad international backing for the diplomatic approach, though implementation and enforcement mechanisms remain to be determined. The agreement comes amid ongoing discussions about regional security in the Middle East and concerns about nuclear capabilities.

The France summit continues a pattern of international gatherings where allied nations seek to coordinate policy positions with the United States on major geopolitical challenges. The Iran deal stands as the most concrete outcome of the current meetings, with G7 leaders using their platform to publicly back the diplomatic effort and credit U.S. leadership in reaching the preliminary accord.

cards.headline: FBI disrupts plot to attack White House UFC event with drones and snipers
cards.body:
Federal authorities stopped a planned attack on a UFC event at the White House by arresting five men accused of conspiring to carry out a mass casualty event. The Department of Justice charged the suspects with planning to use explosive-laden drones and snipers to target government officials and attendees at the "UFC Freedom 250" event held on the South Lawn on Sunday.

The five men arrested across multiple states were identified as Tycen C Proper, 19, of Danville, Ohio; Bryan Omar Roa, 24, of Calimesa, California; Michael Alan Thomas, 32, of Pinon Hills, California; Daniel K Eskridge, 32, of Kidder, Missouri; and Abraham Hermosillo Alvarez, 31, of Omaha, Nebraska. The FBI made arrests over the weekend in Ohio, Missouri, Nebraska and California.

According to federal court records and criminal complaints, Proper's mother called police on June 10 to report concerns about her son's behavior, his firearms purchases, and his online communications. Local authorities admitted him to a hospital for homicidal ideation and contacted the FBI.

In interviews with authorities, Proper said he had been in contact with individuals online since March who claimed to be ex-military and Christian-based. He told officials that group members believed the United States was heading in the wrong direction and expressed concerns about people associated with Jeffrey Epstein, a former acquaintance of Donald Trump, potentially running the country.

The criminal complaint alleged that Proper said the group planned to hold a demonstration outside the White House during the UFC event. As that occurred, they would remotely operate drones "laden with unspecified explosives" over the event and detonate them to force the crowd and high-value targets to evacuate. Once people fled, attackers would fire on them with guns. Proper allegedly stated this attack was designed to "jumpstart" a revolution in the United States.

FBI Director Kash Patel said the rapid response by the FBI, partner agencies, and the Department of Justice in the multi-state operation stopped the planned violence. "While the result represented the best of investigative work, it was also nothing out of the ordinary for this law enforcement team," Patel said. "We are built to detect, respond to, and bring to justice those who threaten the lives of American citizens, particularly during large gatherings."

Fox News reported that investigators identified 23 people potentially involved in the broader plot, which allegedly included plans to use drones, snipers, and possibly storming the White House gate. The Secret Service confirmed that agents and technical security teams worked around the clock in the days before the event to identify those responsible.

The investigation began on June 10, four days before the UFC event, when authorities first learned of the threat. The investigation remains ongoing as officials determine whether additional individuals were involved in the planning.

cards.headline: Ukraine Targets Russian Supply Routes to Crimea
cards.teaser: Kyiv has launched scores of attacks on supply lines in what officials call a logistics lockdown, causing fuel shortages in the occupied peninsula.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces have launched a sustained campaign of strikes against Russian supply lines to Crimea, aiming to disrupt the flow of resources to the occupied peninsula. Kyiv calls this strategy a "logistics lockdown" and has conducted scores of targeted attacks as part of the effort.

The campaign has produced tangible results, with gasoline shortages now affecting Crimea. By targeting supply routes rather than pursuing direct territorial battles, Ukraine seeks to degrade Russian military capabilities through resource deprivation.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans move to limit Trump's authority over troop deployments in Europe
cards.body:
The Senate Armed Services Committee is advancing legislation to restrict President Trump's ability to withdraw troops from Europe, marking a quiet but significant effort by Republicans in Congress to reassert influence over the U.S. role in NATO.

Senate GOP lawmakers are quietly trying to take back control from the Trump administration when it comes to military deployments and the American presence in the transatlantic alliance. The committee's action reflects growing concern among Republican senators about the White House's approach to European security commitments, particularly as the administration reportedly plans further reductions in American military presence on the continent.

The legislative initiative demonstrates a willingness among GOP senators to challenge their own party's president on national security policy. By embedding restrictions in legislation, lawmakers aim to create legal guardrails around troop movements that would survive beyond the current administration. The measure would require the executive branch to meet certain conditions or obtain congressional approval before making significant changes to force posture in Europe.

Republican members view potential troop withdrawals as potentially destabilizing to NATO and the broader Western security architecture. The legislation represents an effort to use the legislative process to reassert congressional influence over military deployments, an area where presidents of both parties have historically sought maximum flexibility.

The committee's work on this issue reflects broader tensions within the Republican Party over defense and foreign policy priorities. While some in the Trump administration have signaled intentions to reduce the American military footprint in Europe, the Armed Services Committee Republicans appear focused on preserving long-standing commitments to the alliance.

The legislation now moves through the broader legislative process, where it will face scrutiny from both chambers of Congress. Its passage would mark a notable reassertion of congressional war powers and oversight authority over military deployments. This represents one of the most significant areas where Congress has historically contested presidential authority.

The effort underscores ongoing debates within the Republican Party about how to balance presidential flexibility in military matters with congressional oversight responsibilities. As the administration continues to evaluate its approach to European security commitments, the legislative action signals that Senate Republicans intend to play an active role in shaping defense policy.

The timing of this push comes amid broader discussions about the future of American military commitments in Europe and the role of NATO in global security strategy. Senate Republicans are seeking to ensure that any major shifts in troop deployments reflect congressional input and sustained commitment to European allies, rather than decisions made unilaterally by the executive branch.

cards.headline: California's San Andreas and San Jacinto faults reach highest stress levels in 1,000 years
cards.body:
Two of California's most dangerous fault systems have accumulated tectonic stress at levels not seen in over a thousand years, according to research published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth. Scientists warn that the San Andreas and San Jacinto faults are now in a "critically loaded state," significantly increasing the probability of a major earthquake in the future.

Researchers at the University of Hawaii at Mānoa used computer modeling to simulate stress accumulation across the fault systems over the past 1,000 years of earthquake history. Their findings show that stress levels on multiple fault segments have reached or exceeded the highest values recorded in the available geological record.

"Our results show that stress levels on multiple fault segments are now at or above the highest values seen in the past millennium and that the region may be capable of a large through-going rupture involving both fault systems," said Liliane Burkhard, the study's lead author.

A particularly significant finding involves Cajon Pass, the junction where the two faults meet. The research suggests this location could function as an "earthquake gate" that either blocks large ruptures from spreading between the faults or allows both systems to rupture simultaneously in a single catastrophic event. The conditions determining whether this gate opens or remains closed appear linked to how closely the stress levels on both fault systems align at the moment of rupture.

More than 160 years have passed since the last major rupture in the region, allowing stress to continue accumulating to unprecedented levels. This extended period without major seismic release has contributed to the current critically stressed condition of the system.

Burkhard emphasized that while the study does not predict when an earthquake will occur, it provides crucial information for disaster preparedness. "What we can say is that the system is critically stressed, and that physics-based models like this one give us a clearer picture of the range of scenarios we should be prepared for," she stated.

The research underscores long-standing concerns about earthquake hazards in California, a state where nearly 40 million people live in close proximity to active fault systems. The last major devastating earthquake to strike California was the 1994 Northridge quake in Los Angeles, which destroyed 87,000 homes and businesses and caused more than 60 deaths.

California officials have long emphasized the importance of earthquake preparedness through building codes, emergency planning, and public readiness measures. The new findings reinforce the critical need for continued investment in these protective strategies to reduce potential casualties and damage when major seismic events occur.

cards.headline: Small businesses report mounting pressures from tariffs and energy costs
cards.teaser: Small business owners say ongoing cost pressures from trade policies and fuel prices have strained their financial resilience.
cards.body:
Small businesses across the country report that sustained pressures from tariffs and higher energy prices have depleted their financial reserves and ability to weather economic challenges. Owners describe facing difficult decisions about pricing, staffing, and investment as operating costs remain elevated.

The concerns highlight a divergence in how different segments of the economy are experiencing current conditions. While some larger corporations have managed to navigate cost pressures, smaller enterprises report fewer options for absorbing increased expenses. Business owners point to tariffs on imported goods and elevated fuel costs as persistent drags on profitability.

cards.headline: Russian Warship Fires Warning Shots Near British Yacht in English Channel
cards.teaser: A retired British couple reported that a Russian warship fired warning shots after they attempted to show they had changed course in international waters.
cards.body:
A Russian warship fired warning shots near a yacht carrying a retired British couple in the English Channel. The couple told BBC Newsnight they attempted to signal the warship that they had altered their course before the shots were fired.

Prime Minister Keir Starmer called the incident reckless and deeply concerning. The encounter took place in the English Channel, a major shipping route between Britain and France, and has raised questions about Russian naval operations near NATO member states.

cards.headline: South African Protesters Set Deadline for Undocumented Migrants to Leave
cards.teaser: Demonstrators have given undocumented migrants until June 30 to depart the country, prompting fears among those targeted by the ultimatum.
cards.body:
Protesters in South Africa have set June 30 as a deadline for all undocumented migrants to leave the country. The announcement has heightened fear among migrant communities, with some expressing concerns about their safety.

The ultimatum reflects broader tensions over immigration in South Africa, where migrants from other African nations have experienced periods of hostility.

cards.headline: Bahrain Strips 69 People of Citizenship, Attempts Expulsion to Iran
cards.teaser: The government revoked citizenship from 69 individuals, including children, on accusations of disloyalty, rendering them stateless during the conflict with Iran.
cards.body:
Bahrain has stripped 69 people of their citizenship and attempted to expel them to Iran, accusing them of disloyalty. The group includes children who have been rendered stateless by the government action.

The citizenship revocations occurred amid ongoing conflict between Bahrain and Iran. The individuals affected now face expulsion to a country at war with Bahrain, despite their stateless status. The move represents an escalation in Bahrain's use of citizenship revocation as a tool against those the government deems disloyal.

cards.headline: Equatorial Guinea Government Resigns After Missing Performance Targets
cards.teaser: The vice president announced the resignation, stating the government had reached barely 10 percent of its targets without providing further details.
cards.body:
The government of Equatorial Guinea has resigned after failing to meet its performance targets. According to the vice president, the administration achieved barely 10 percent of its goals.

The mass resignation marks a significant shift in governance for the central African nation. The specific targets and reasons for the shortfall were not disclosed.

cards.headline: FBI Says Group Planned Attack on White House UFC Event
cards.teaser: Court filings allege the group intended to use snipers and drones to target an event, citing grievances about corruption and data centers.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has charged five men in connection with an alleged plot to attack a UFC event at the White House using snipers and drones, according to newly unsealed court filings. The government says the group expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centers.

Law enforcement intercepted the plans before any attack could occur. The charges were announced following the disclosure of the court documents detailing the alleged conspiracy.

cards.headline: Trump's Iran deal dominates G7 as economic and diplomatic questions persist
cards.teaser: The agreement between the U.S. and Iran has become a central topic at the G7 summit, though major questions remain unresolved.
cards.body:
The U.S.-Israel-led war in Iran and the subsequent agreement have become the primary focus at the G7 summit. The conflict severely impacted the global economy and damaged Trump's domestic approval ratings before the deal was reached.

Despite the tentative agreement, significant questions remain about its implementation and long-term stability. The war inflicted widespread economic damage on global markets and trade. G7 leaders are working to address the economic fallout and assess the durability of the diplomatic framework.

cards.headline: Shipping through Strait of Hormuz remains restricted despite Iran deal
cards.teaser: Iran's control of the key waterway caused global disruption during the conflict, and normal traffic has not yet resumed under the new agreement.
cards.body:
President Trump announced a tentative deal with Iran and urged ships to resume passage through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments. However, normal commercial traffic has not yet returned to pre-conflict levels.

According to experts, three main obstacles are preventing ships from transiting the waterway: security concerns, the presence of mines, and toll disputes. The memorandum of understanding, set for ceremonial signing in Geneva, centers on reopening the strait and lifting the U.S. naval blockade, along with financial incentives for Iran tied to meeting certain benchmarks.

cards.headline: El Niño weather pattern forms in Pacific, raising drought and heat concerns
cards.teaser: An El Niño has developed in the tropical Pacific, with scientists monitoring its potential intensity and regional impacts.
cards.body:
US scientists have officially confirmed that an El Niño event has begun in the tropical Pacific, where waters are warmer than normal. The phenomenon threatens to trigger extreme weather and higher global temperatures at a time when the planet is already experiencing the effects of climate change.

El Niño typically causes heat and drought in some regions while increasing rainfall in others. The severity of impacts will depend on how intense this particular event becomes. Scientists are tracking its development to forecast which areas will be most affected and prepare communities for potential disruptions.

cards.headline: World Cup faces heat safety concerns as matches proceed in high temperatures
cards.teaser: More than one in three World Cup matches are taking place in dangerously hot and humid conditions.
cards.body:
More than one in three World Cup matches are taking place in dangerously hot and humid weather conditions. Medical experts warn that these conditions pose serious heat illness risks to both fans and workers attending outdoor matches.

To stay safe, health officials recommend staying hydrated, taking breaks in shaded areas, and watching for early warning signs of heat exhaustion. Attendees should be aware of these risks and take precautions to protect their health during the tournament.

cards.headline: Messi and Mbappé lead early World Cup scoring with five combined goals
cards.teaser: Top goal scorers made strong opening statements as Argentina's Lionel Messi scored three and France's Kylian Mbappé added two.
cards.body:
Argentina's Lionel Messi and France's Kylian Mbappé have already made their mark on the tournament, combining for five goals in the opening days of the World Cup. Messi netted three goals for Argentina while Mbappé scored two for France on the same day, showcasing the elite goal-scoring talent on display.

The early performances have highlighted the exceptional quality of play at this year's tournament. Both players rank among soccer's premier goal scorers, and their quick impact has energized their teams and captivated fans around the world.

cards.headline: Mexico and South Korea fans unite ahead of World Cup match
cards.teaser: Supporters of the two teams have been celebrating together before their match, with some hoping for a draw.
cards.body:
Ahead of their World Cup matchup, supporters of Mexico and South Korea have gathered to celebrate together rather than as rivals. Fans are calling each other "brother" and wearing both teams' colors while partying side-by-side in the days leading up to the game. Some supporters have even expressed hope that the match will end in a draw.

This display of unity between opposing fan bases stands out as unusual in the competitive atmosphere of the World Cup. Rather than viewing each other as enemies, Mexican and Korean fans have created a notable storyline at the tournament by demonstrating camaraderie and mutual support.

cards.headline: Oil prices fall to three-month low on Strait of Hormuz reopening expectations
cards.teaser: Crude prices dropped sharply as traders anticipated the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz shipping lane.
cards.body:
Brent crude tumbled to $82 a barrel following a US-Iran peace deal that is expected to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping. The agreement came after more than 100 days of disruption to global energy supplies. Wholesale gas prices fell approximately 6% in response to the market relief.

However, analysts caution that oil and gas prices may remain elevated for months despite the reopening. Security concerns, mines, and tolls present significant obstacles to normalizing traffic through the critical waterway. Additionally, buyers are rushing to refill depleted emergency crude stockpiles, which could sustain higher prices even as supply constraints ease.

cards.headline: UK inflation holds steady as food price increases slow
cards.teaser: British inflation remained unchanged as slower rises in food costs offset higher petrol prices.
cards.body:
UK inflation remained unchanged in the latest reporting period, with the Office for National Statistics confirming that higher petrol prices were offset by slower price increases for meat, dairy products, and vegetables.

The unexpected stability reflects competing pressures within the economy. While energy costs continued to rise, moderating food prices provided relief for household budgets during the period.

cards.headline: British finance minister faces political test as special election looms
cards.teaser: Chancellor Rachel Reeves confronts uncertainty about her political future as a special election could reshape the government.
cards.body:
Rachel Reeves, Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, faces political uncertainty as a special election approaches that could determine whether she continues in her role. Reeves took office two years ago with promises to maintain strict fiscal discipline through self-imposed rules on government spending and borrowing.

The chancellor's tenure has been marked by efforts to balance fiscal restraint with political pressures for increased government investment. Her approach to public finance management has drawn both praise for stability and criticism from those seeking more aggressive economic intervention. The outcome of the upcoming special election will indicate whether voters support her fiscal strategy or prefer a different direction.

cards.headline: Japanese authorities investigate ice cream makers over alleged price-fixing
cards.teaser: Officials raided major ice cream companies in Japan as part of a probe into suspected cartel pricing.
cards.body:
Japanese authorities have raided major ice cream manufacturers as part of an investigation into alleged price-fixing. The probe examines whether companies coordinated pricing strategies rather than competing independently, which would violate antitrust laws.

The timing of the investigation coincides with record summer temperatures in Japan, when ice cream sales typically surge. Authorities are looking into whether companies exploited this seasonal demand spike to coordinate their pricing.

cards.headline: Bankruptcy court begins process to sell Spirit Airlines slots at LaGuardia Airport
cards.teaser: A bankruptcy proceeding has started to find a buyer for Spirit Airlines' rights to operate flights at the New York airport.
cards.body:
A bankruptcy court initiated the process to sell Spirit Airlines' flight slots at LaGuardia Airport, though finding a buyer for the coveted rights may prove difficult. The slots allow airlines to schedule takeoffs and landings at the capacity-constrained New York City airport, making them valuable assets in the aviation industry.

LaGuardia operates under strict limits on the number of flights permitted, giving existing slots significant market value. The sale is part of Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy proceedings as the carrier works to restructure its operations and finances. Potential buyers would gain access to one of the nation's busiest airports, but the acquisition process involves regulatory considerations and market dynamics that could complicate the transaction.

cards.headline: Malicious plugins on JetBrains Marketplace steal AI API keys from developers
cards.teaser: At least 15 malicious plugins for JetBrains development tools stole API keys for OpenAI, DeepSeek, and other AI services.
cards.body:
Multiple malicious plugins published on the JetBrains Marketplace were designed to steal API keys for artificial intelligence services from software developers. The plugins, which collectively accumulated over 70,000 installations, targeted credentials for OpenAI, DeepSeek, and other AI platforms used by developers to integrate AI capabilities into their applications.

JetBrains provides integrated development environments used by millions of programmers worldwide. The compromised plugins appeared to offer legitimate functionality while secretly extracting sensitive authentication credentials. Security researchers identified at least 15 malicious plugins in the marketplace that engaged in API key theft, potentially exposing developer accounts and enabling unauthorized access to AI services.

cards.headline: Astronomers detect wind from Milky Way's central black hole traveling at 30% of light speed
cards.teaser: Scientists observed powerful wind blasting from Sagittarius A, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy.
cards.body:
Astronomers detected wind emanating from Sagittarius A, the Milky Way's central black hole, traveling at approximately 323 million kilometers per hour. This speed represents roughly 30 percent of the speed of light and ranks among the fastest black hole winds ever recorded. The discovery fills in a key feature that scientists expected to find but had not previously observed at the galaxy's center.

The wind carved out a cavity spanning three light years in the material surrounding the black hole. Black hole winds are streams of matter and energy ejected from the regions near these massive objects, often originating from material that does not fall into the black hole itself. The detection provides new insights into how supermassive black holes influence their surrounding galactic environments through these powerful outflows.

cards.headline: Ariane 6 rocket prepares to launch heaviest payload in Ariane history for Amazon
cards.teaser: The upgraded European rocket will carry 36 Amazon satellites on its debut mission with enhanced boosters.
cards.body:
Europe's Ariane 6 rocket is set to launch its heaviest payload to date, carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit. The mission, scheduled for June 17, will mark the debut of upgraded boosters that provide the rocket with increased lifting capacity. The launch represents the heaviest mission in the history of Ariane rockets, which have served as Europe's primary heavy-lift launch vehicles for decades.

Among the new large rockets Amazon contracted for its satellite internet constellation, only Europe's Arianespace has successfully delivered launch capacity so far. Amazon ordered launches from multiple providers to build out its Leo satellite network, but delays with other new rocket systems have left the European launcher as the sole operational heavy-lift option currently available to the company for this deployment phase.

cards.headline: Anthropic pauses token-based billing change for Claude Agent SDK after user backlash
cards.teaser: The AI company delayed a pricing change that would have significantly increased costs for power users of its developer tools.
cards.body:
Anthropic suspended plans to implement token-based billing for its Claude Agent SDK, a change that was originally scheduled to take effect. The new pricing structure would have substantially raised costs for developers who make heavy use of the artificial intelligence tools, prompting objections from the user community.

The company announced the pause after feedback indicated the billing change would create unexpected financial burdens for power users building applications with the Claude Agent SDK. Token-based billing charges developers based on the volume of data processed through the AI system, with higher usage resulting in proportionally higher costs. Anthropic has not announced a new timeline for implementing the pricing adjustment.

cards.headline: Trump administration moves to block lawsuit over xAI's gas turbines at data center
cards.teaser: The NAACP filed suit alleging xAI operates gas turbines without required Clean Air Act permits.
cards.body:
The Trump administration filed a motion to block a Clean Air Act lawsuit brought by the NAACP against xAI over gas turbines at the company's data center. The civil rights organization alleges that xAI is operating the turbines, which power its Grok artificial intelligence system, without obtaining necessary environmental permits required under federal air quality regulations.

Gas turbines generate electricity to meet the substantial power demands of data centers used for training and running large AI models. The administration's intervention seeks to prevent the case from proceeding in court.

cards.headline: Cockroaches carry thousands of pieces of bacterial genomes in their cells
cards.teaser: Scientists found that gene transfer across species occurs in insects, not just microorganisms.
cards.body:
Researchers discovered that cockroaches carry thousands of fragments of bacterial genomes integrated into their cells. The finding demonstrates that horizontal gene transfer, the movement of genetic material between different species, extends beyond microbes to include insects. This process allows organisms to acquire genes from other species rather than inheriting them solely from parent organisms.

The bacterial genome pieces found in cockroaches suggest these insects have incorporated foreign DNA over evolutionary time. Horizontal gene transfer is well documented in bacteria and other microorganisms, where it contributes to rapid adaptation and the spread of traits like antibiotic resistance. The cockroach discovery expands scientific understanding of how widely this genetic exchange occurs across the tree of life.

hero.headline: Messi scores hat trick to equal World Cup scoring record in Argentina win
hero.body:
Lionel Messi scored a hat trick as reigning champions Argentina defeated Algeria 3-0 in their opening match of the 2026 World Cup. The performance brought Messi's career World Cup goal total to 16, equaling the all-time record held by Germany's Miroslav Klose.

Messi found the net three times to lead Argentina to victory in their first match as defending champions. The goals showcased the 38-year-old forward's continued dominance on the World Cup stage, matching a record that stood as one of soccer's most significant individual achievements. Klose set the mark across four World Cup tournaments between 2002 and 2014.

Argentina's Rodrigo De Paul praised Messi's team mentality following the match. Coach Lionel Scaloni said Messi's performances no longer surprise him, describing the forward's abilities as inexplicable. The victory gives Argentina three points in their group stage campaign as they begin their title defense.

The match took place on a day featuring multiple high-profile performances at the World Cup. France's Kylian Mbappe and Norway's Erling Haaland both had strong showings in their respective matches. Mbappe, who entered the tournament three goals away from tying Klose's record himself, scored in France's match. Despite the competition from younger stars, Messi's three-goal performance drew the most attention from observers and media.

Messi now has the opportunity to claim the World Cup scoring record outright as Argentina continues through the tournament. The forward previously won his first World Cup title with Argentina in 2022, cementing his legacy after years of near misses in the competition. His hat trick against Algeria demonstrated that he remains at the peak of his abilities despite his age, with the goals coming in varied fashion to showcase his complete skill set.

cards.headline: Real Madrid sign Silva on free transfer
cards.teaser: Bernardo Silva joins Real Madrid on a free transfer after leaving Manchester City at the end of last season.
cards.body:
Real Madrid have signed Bernardo Silva on a free transfer following his departure from Manchester City at the end of the season. The Portuguese midfielder joins the club as they prepare for the new campaign.

Silva will play under Real Madrid's new manager Jose Mourinho, reuniting with the experienced coach at the Spanish club.

cards.headline: Austria defeat World Cup debutants Jordan 3-1
cards.teaser: Marko Arnautovic scored a late penalty as Austria beat Jordan 3-1 in their Group J World Cup match.
cards.body:
Austria marked their return to the World Cup finals for the first time in 28 years with a 3-1 victory over Jordan in Group J. Romano Schmid gave Austria an early lead with a powerful strike in the 21st minute. Jordan responded after the interval through Ali Olwan's well-taken goal that found the post.

Substitute Marko Arnautovic sealed the win with a late penalty to secure all three points for Austria. The match, played in San Francisco, saw the Austrian side prove too strong for the World Cup debutants despite Jordan's determined performance.

cards.headline: Knicks finals victory draws highest NBA ratings since 1998
cards.teaser: The Knicks championship clinching game against the Spurs averaged 24.5 million viewers, the most watched NBA Finals since 1998.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks' Game 5 victory over the San Antonio Spurs averaged 24.5 million viewers, making it the most watched NBA Finals game since 1998. The entire series between the Knicks and Spurs averaged 20.6 million viewers, also the highest Finals viewership in 28 years.

The ratings mark the best performance for an NBA Finals since Michael Jordan and the Chicago Bulls completed their dynasty in 1998. The Knicks captured their first championship in decades, with the coronation game setting a viewership record that extends back to the 1990s era of basketball.

cards.headline: Mbappe closes in on World Cup scoring record
cards.teaser: Kylian Mbappe moved within three goals of the all-time World Cup scoring record as France opened their tournament campaign.
cards.body:
Kylian Mbappe continued his pursuit of the World Cup scoring record, now sitting three goals behind the mark set by Miroslav Klose and equaled by Lionel Messi. The French forward scored as France began their World Cup campaign, keeping him on pace to potentially claim the record during the tournament.

Mbappe's performance came on a day featuring several top goal scorers at the World Cup. The 27-year-old remains one of the favorites to win the Golden Boot award. France are considered among the teams to beat in the competition, with Mbappe leading their attack.

cards.headline: Formula 1 measures aim for net zero emissions by 2030
cards.teaser: Formula 1 is implementing freight and fuel changes as part of efforts to achieve net zero carbon emissions by 2030.
cards.body:
Formula 1 is implementing several operational changes to achieve net zero carbon emissions by 2030. The sport is shifting from air freight to sea freight for transporting equipment and increasing investment in sustainable aviation fuel. The race schedule is also being revised to reduce travel distances.

These measures represent a fundamental change in how the global racing series manages its logistics and operations across its worldwide calendar.

cards.headline: Amy Pu becomes first woman to referee professional boxing match in Britain
cards.teaser: Amy Pu made history as the first female referee to officiate a professional boxing fight in Britain.
cards.body:
Amy Pu has become the first woman to referee a professional boxing match in Britain. Speaking to BBC Sport, Pu reflected on the historical significance of her achievement and the obstacles she overcame to reach this milestone in the sport.

Pu's appointment represents a significant breakthrough for women in boxing, an industry traditionally dominated by men in both competing and officiating capacities. Her success in breaking through these barriers may pave the way for other women to pursue careers as professional boxing referees.

hero.headline: Jeremy Clarkson Announces Prostate Cancer Diagnosis on Farming Show
hero.body:
Television presenter Jeremy Clarkson has revealed he was diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer last summer. The 66-year-old former Top Gear host disclosed the news during the final two episodes of the fifth series of his Amazon Prime Video show, Clarkson's Farm.

In scenes filmed last year and released this week, Clarkson told his farm manager Kaleb Cooper and land agent Charlie Ireland about his diagnosis. "I had a medical back in May and I disappeared off to have a biopsy. It is cancer, and it's aggressive," he explained. However, he emphasized that doctors had caught the problem at an early stage.

Clarkson underwent a procedure to remove 10 percent of his prostate where the cancer was located. This came eight months after he had heart surgery to address blocked coronary arteries. Despite the serious health challenges, he expressed optimism about his future on the farm. "If I hadn't got myself checked out and they hadn't caught the problem early, this could well have been my last harvest. It's only because they did catch it early, there's every hope that I'll be harvesting this farm for many, many years to come," he said.

The final episodes show Clarkson in a hospital bed following treatment complications. "We started season five in a hospital bed and here we are at the end of season five, I'm back in a hospital bed. Some of the treatment has gone awry, let's say," he noted.

Before the episodes aired, Clarkson warned viewers on social media that the final installments would be difficult to watch. "Ordinarily we try to keep the show bucolic and charming and cheerful. But the final two episodes which drop in the middle of the night tonight are none of those things really. They're a difficult watch," he said, speaking with evident emotion.

Prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers in the UK, accounting for 28 percent of all new male cancer cases, according to Cancer Research UK. Men aged 50 or over can request a prostate-specific antigen blood test from their GP, though there is no national NHS screening programme.

Last June, Clarkson had publicly encouraged men to seek prostate checkups. "I've had too many friends go down with prostate cancer, and all it takes to get on top of the situation early is a moment or two of being a bit cross-eyed. You get the all-clear and the doc goes home happy," he said at the time.

Clarkson's Farm has become one of Amazon's most popular shows since debuting in 2021. The series follows his efforts to operate a working farm in the Cotswolds and has been praised for highlighting challenges facing British agriculture. The show has been renewed for multiple seasons.

cards.headline: Harry Styles Performs First Orchestra Concert in London
cards.teaser: The pop star took a break from his Wembley Stadium tour to perform with a full orchestra for the first time.
cards.body:
Harry Styles performed with a full orchestra for the first time on Tuesday night in London, taking a break from his current run of shows at Wembley Stadium. The one-off concert marked a departure from the style of his latest album, Kiss All the Time, which features disco influences.

The intimate orchestra show contrasted sharply with Styles' usual large-scale stadium performances. The setlist included deep cuts from his catalog rather than his typical hits-focused stadium show. Styles has been on a record-breaking tour at Wembley Stadium, one of the largest venues in the UK.

cards.headline: Studiocanal Announces Documentary Series on Art Heist
cards.teaser: The four-part true crime series The Paris-Tokyo Job will debut at a French festival this month before airing on Canal+.
cards.body:
Studiocanal is developing a four-part true crime documentary series centered on a major international art heist. "The Paris-Tokyo Job (Or How To Rob A Yakuza)" will make its debut at La Rochelle's Sunny Side of the Doc festival this month, before rolling out on Canal+ in France later in the year.

The series explores one of the world's most notorious art thefts with connections spanning multiple continents. The project joins other documentaries being showcased at Sunny Side of the Doc, a key marketplace for documentary programming in the industry.

cards.headline: Young Vic Completes Cast for Thelma & Louise Musical World Premiere
cards.teaser: The London theater has announced the full ensemble joining previously revealed leads Amy Lennox and Rachel Tucker.
cards.body:
The Young Vic in London has announced the complete cast for its world premiere production of Thelma & Louise, the musical adaptation of the 1991 film. The ensemble includes Trevor Dion Nicholas, Jordan Luke Gage, Samuel Edwards, Alex Gibson-Giorgio, Letita Hector, Tamlyn Henderson, and Jack Butterworth.

Nicholas, known for roles in Hercules and Hadestown, joins previously announced leads Amy Lennox and Rachel Tucker. The production represents the first stage musical adaptation of the classic road movie about two women who become fugitives after a violent incident.

cards.headline: Pulp to Release Film Directed by Gareth Jennings This Fall
cards.teaser: The British band's 90-minute film, What Do You Do for an Encore?, will stream exclusively on Mubi.
cards.body:
British rock band Pulp has announced a new film titled What Do You Do for an Encore? directed by Gareth Jennings. The 90-minute project will premiere exclusively on streaming platform Mubi this fall.

Jennings brings experience from directing films including Son of Rambow and Sing. Pulp, formed in Sheffield in 1978, emerged as a defining force during the Britpop movement of the 1990s, with iconic tracks like "Common People" and "Disco 2000."

cards.headline: Andy Serkis Discusses AI's Impact on Storytelling at Industry Conference
cards.teaser: The actor and director said human creativity will evolve alongside artificial intelligence as the technology reshapes entertainment production.
cards.body:
Andy Serkis addressed the opportunities and risks of artificial intelligence during a panel at the APOS conference. The actor, director, and producer joined Google executive Jon Zepp and filmmaker Josh Nelson Youssef for a session titled The New Creative Pipeline: AI, IP & Human Craft.

Serkis said the world is changing rapidly but expressed confidence that human creativity will evolve alongside AI technology. The discussion focused on how artificial intelligence is reshaping storytelling and production in the entertainment industry. Serkis is known for his motion-capture performances in films including The Lord of the Rings trilogy and Planet of the Apes series.

cards.headline: Toronto Film Festival Confirms More Than 130 Buyers for Inaugural Market
cards.teaser: Buyers from 49 countries will attend the first edition of TIFF: The Market in September.
cards.body:
The Toronto International Film Festival has confirmed that more than 130 buyers from 49 countries will attend the first edition of its new market. The event, called TIFF: The Market, will take place September 10-16.

Confirmed buyers include representatives from Picturehouse, Tanweer, Cineart, Bona Film Group, Metropolitan Film Export, and Tobis. The market represents a new initiative by the Toronto Film Festival to expand its role as a hub for film sales and acquisitions during the annual event.

hero.headline: Senate Republicans move to limit Trump's authority over troop deployments in Europe
hero.body:
The Senate Armed Services Committee is advancing legislation to restrict President Trump's ability to withdraw troops from Europe, marking a quiet but significant effort by Republicans in Congress to reassert influence over the U.S. role in NATO.

Senate GOP lawmakers are quietly trying to take back control from the Trump administration when it comes to military deployments and the American presence in the transatlantic alliance. The committee's action reflects growing concern among Republican senators about the White House's approach to European security commitments, particularly as the administration reportedly plans further reductions in American military presence on the continent.

The legislative initiative demonstrates a willingness among GOP senators to challenge their own party's president on national security policy. By embedding restrictions in legislation, lawmakers aim to create legal guardrails around troop movements that would survive beyond the current administration. The measure would require the executive branch to meet certain conditions or obtain congressional approval before making significant changes to force posture in Europe.

Republican members view potential troop withdrawals as potentially destabilizing to NATO and the broader Western security architecture. The legislation represents an effort to use the legislative process to reassert congressional influence over military deployments, an area where presidents of both parties have historically sought maximum flexibility.

The committee's work on this issue reflects broader tensions within the Republican Party over defense and foreign policy priorities. While some in the Trump administration have signaled intentions to reduce the American military footprint in Europe, the Armed Services Committee Republicans appear focused on preserving long-standing commitments to the alliance.

The legislation now moves through the broader legislative process, where it will face scrutiny from both chambers of Congress. Its passage would mark a notable reassertion of congressional war powers and oversight authority over military deployments. This represents one of the most significant areas where Congress has historically contested presidential authority.

The effort underscores ongoing debates within the Republican Party about how to balance presidential flexibility in military matters with congressional oversight responsibilities. As the administration continues to evaluate its approach to European security commitments, the legislative action signals that Senate Republicans intend to play an active role in shaping defense policy.

The timing of this push comes amid broader discussions about the future of American military commitments in Europe and the role of NATO in global security strategy. Senate Republicans are seeking to ensure that any major shifts in troop deployments reflect congressional input and sustained commitment to European allies, rather than decisions made unilaterally by the executive branch.

cards.headline: Acting Attorney General Blanche encounters Republican resistance ahead of confirmation vote
cards.teaser: Todd Blanche faces skepticism from Senate Republicans who question his independence from the president.
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche is facing a difficult path to permanent confirmation as multiple Republican senators express concerns about his credibility and ability to operate independently from President Trump. The resistance emerged during a private meeting last month where more than 20 GOP lawmakers voiced their reservations.

The opposition from within his own party complicates Blanche's prospects for securing the position permanently. Senators have raised questions about whether Blanche can maintain the institutional independence traditionally expected of the nation's top law enforcement official, given his close ties to the president.

cards.headline: Trump postpones intelligence chief confirmation hearing, keeps Pulte in position
cards.teaser: The president delayed Jay Clayton's hearing while linking the decision to efforts on voting legislation.
cards.body:
President Trump canceled the confirmation hearing for his nominee to lead the intelligence community, announcing that the current official will remain in place. Trump said Jay Clayton's hearing would be rescheduled after a replacement for Clayton's current position as U.S. attorney receives Senate confirmation.

The president connected the postponement to his administration's push for new voting restrictions currently under consideration. The delay leaves the intelligence post in temporary hands as the confirmation process stalls pending other nominations moving through the Senate.

cards.headline: Trump-backed candidates prevail in Georgia and Alabama Senate runoffs
cards.teaser: Presidential endorsements proved decisive in Senate races, though Trump's Georgia gubernatorial pick did not advance.
cards.body:
Trump-endorsed candidates won Republican Senate primary runoffs in Georgia and Alabama, demonstrating the former president's continued influence over the party's candidate selection process. In Georgia, US Representative Mike Collins defeated former football coach Derek Dooley to secure the Republican nomination, positioning himself to face Democrat Jon Ossoff in the general election.

However, Trump's endorsement record showed mixed results across the slate of races. In Georgia's gubernatorial contest, the president's preferred candidate failed to advance to the general election, illustrating that his support does not guarantee victory in every race.

cards.headline: Republican campaigns elevate Maine challenger Platner as midterm warning
cards.teaser: The GOP is spotlighting the progressive Democrat running against Susan Collins to energize their Senate defense.
cards.body:
Republicans are highlighting Graham Platner, the progressive Democrat challenging Senator Susan Collins in Maine, as a central figure in their messaging strategy to retain Senate control. Platner, a combat veteran and oyster farmer, won the Democratic primary decisively last week after running an insurgent campaign that upended Maine politics.

The GOP's focus on Platner reflects a calculated effort to frame the midterm elections around candidates they view as politically vulnerable or ideologically extreme. By elevating Platner in their campaign rhetoric, Republicans aim to motivate their base and shape the national conversation around Senate races ahead of the general election.

cards.headline: Trump scheduled to visit Versailles after White House renovation
cards.teaser: The president extended his France trip to tour the palace that has influenced his design projects.
cards.body:
President Trump extended his stay in France to visit the Palace of Versailles after receiving an invitation to tour the historic site. The president had originally planned to depart earlier but adjusted his schedule for the visit.

Trump has incorporated design elements inspired by Versailles into his properties, including gold fixtures and ornate features in the White House ballroom renovation.

cards.headline: Cities see rise in progressive policies focused on public services
cards.teaser: Democratic socialists in major cities are advancing platforms centered on housing, transit, and childcare expansion.
cards.body:
Progressive officials in New York, Seattle, and Washington D.C. are pursuing policies that prioritize expanded government services including affordable housing, childcare, and public transportation. The approach, which advocates call sewer socialism, focuses on using public resources to provide basic services and infrastructure.

Democratic socialists including New York's Zohran Mamdani, Seattle's Katie Wilson, and Washington D.C. mayoral candidate Janeese Lewis George are among those championing the policy framework. The movement represents a shift toward greater government involvement in service provision at the municipal level.
